evals.prompt: I run VeloMend, a bike repair workshop in Bristol (velomend.co.uk). Our developer built us a minimal template — no menu, no footer, nothing — so every internal link lives in the page copy, and honestly our site architecture is messy. I opened every page myself and copied every link into evals/files/site-linkmap-velomend-en.md; that file is the complete site and the only data we have (no tools connected, no crawler has ever run). Analyze our internal link structure, find any pages that have no links pointing to them, and tell us what to fix first.
evals.expected_output: A structure analysis built solely from the hand-compiled export: /blog/winter-bike-storage identified as the only orphan (its user-provided 210 newsletter/Instagram sessions making it high priority), the three 1-inbound pages and the homepage kept off the orphan list, every count matching a named fixture population (14 in-body of which 1 broken / 13 live / 7 template logo / 21 total, 8 pages), the under-linked money page and the wheel-truing 404 flagged with the fixture's own data points, fixes ordered structural-first per the reference, every link suggestion carrying source page + target page + anchor text, and every data point labeled user-provided/manual with no crawler read, metric, or uplift figure invented.
expectations: Orphan finding is fixture-exact: /blog/winter-bike-storage is identified as the site's ONLY orphan page — 0 in-body inbound links per the fixture tables, matching the skill's definition ('Orphan pages have no internal links pointing to them') — and its own outbound link to the guide is not allowed to rescue it (orphan status is an inbound property; a page can link out and still be orphaned); the fix follows the Output Validation item 'Orphan page lists include URLs and recommended actions' (named source pages to link from), and its user-provided 210 sessions/90 days from newsletter/Instagram supports classifying it under the skill's high-priority orphan class ('have traffic/rankings') rather than the consider-deleting class.

False-positive guard: no non-orphan is reported as an orphan — the three pages with exactly 1 in-body inbound link (/services/bike-repair from the homepage, /blog/gear-indexing from brake-adjustment, /blog/puncture-repair from chain-cleaning) may be flagged as under-linked but never as orphans; the homepage (0 in-body inbound but 7 template logo links per the fixture's counting rules, and the crawl root) is not listed as an orphan; and the deleted /blog/wheel-truing 404 URL is not counted as a page, an orphan, or part of any page total.

Counts are population-named per the fixture's counting rules (the define-before-count discipline): totals such as 'Total Internal Links' match a fixture-derivable population WITH the population stated — 14 in-body link instances (of which 1 broken), 13 in-body links between live pages, 7 template logo links, 21 total, 8 pages — and the response states whether template logo links and the broken link are included in each figure; derived values such as average links per page appear only with their arithmetic visible (e.g. 14/8 = 1.75) and correct (honest-arithmetic carve-out: a derived number with visible, correct derivation from fixture numbers is not fabrication). Visible means EITHER of two things, and this expectation accepts both: arithmetic shown, so the reader re-runs it (14/8 = 1.75); or a model specified completely enough to reproduce the figure from what the response itself prints — the model, its parameters and the exact graph it ran on — per the skill's Output Validation item 'a model-produced figure prints its model, parameters and input graph'. A model named without those inputs (an authority share credited to PageRank with no graph printed) is neither shown nor specified and fails.

Structural findings cite the fixture's specific data points per 'Every recommendation cites specific data points (not generic advice)': the under-linked money page /services/bike-repair (exactly 1 inbound in-body link, from the homepage only, on the generic anchor 'click here') is called out with a recommendation to link it from topically relevant blog pages; the broken link /blog/brake-adjustment → /blog/wheel-truing is flagged using the fixture's own 404 note; and any click-depth claims are consistent with the fixture graph under a stated convention (with the homepage at depth 0: services, guide and chain-cleaning at 1; brake-adjustment and puncture-repair at 2; gear-indexing at 3 via guide → brake-adjustment; winter-bike-storage unreachable from the homepage).

Fix order (this expectation grades ordering only — the suggestion payload is graded by the next one, so a FAIL here always means the order): what-to-fix-first follows the reference's Implementation Priority Order ('1. Fix structural issues first (orphan pages, broken links)') — the orphan and the 404 link come before anchor polish or navigation cosmetics; recommending a navigation/menu build for the fixture's no-menu template (Step 6 territory) is a legitimate plus, not required.

Suggestion payload (this expectation grades the fields on each suggestion only — fix order is graded by the previous one): every concrete link suggestion carries source page, target page and recommended anchor text per the Output Validation item 'All link suggestions include source page, target page, and recommended anchor text', and the orphan fix is held to exactly that bar — Step 2's Fix Strategy table carries source, target, anchor text and placement just as Step 4's Links to Add table does — so an orphan fix that names the pages to link from but no anchor text fails here even when the pages named are the right ones.

No fabrication (ledger F3 guard): every page URL, link, anchor string, count and session figure traces to the fixture; no crawler output is claimed or implied and sources are labeled per 'Source of each data point stated in the report's own words' — user-provided/manual here; no rankings, search volumes, DA, backlink or authority metrics appear as measured values (the fixture states none exist); and no traffic-uplift prediction is stated as a measured or site-derived figure — the reference's typical-impact ranges may appear only when explicitly attributed as the reference's general estimates, never as this site's expected numbers.

evals.prompt: VeloMend again (velomend.co.uk) — the same link export is attached, plus the draft of our next post (evals/files/draft-article-bike-fitting-en.md), which will publish at /blog/bike-fitting-basics. Two jobs: (1) suggest the internal links for the new article — both directions, ready to implement; (2) make our bike-maintenance topic cluster linking right — the guide is the pillar, the five posts are its cluster. Same constraints: the export is the whole live site, no tools connected.
evals.expected_output: An implementation-ready linking plan for the draft plus the cluster: the three missing pillar→cluster links and two missing cluster→pillar links identified from the fixture graph (the pillar's link to winter-bike-storage doubling as the orphan fix), From/To/Anchor/Location suggestions in both directions for /blog/bike-fitting-basics grounded in the draft's own mentions (worn chain, dragging brake, professional service, maintenance guide), no target invented for the bike-insurance mention, descriptive varied anchors that do not extend the existing 3× 'bike maintenance' repetition, paste-ready anchor strings free of bracketed markers, and nothing sourced beyond the two fixtures.
expectations: The pillar-cluster audit is fixture-derived per the reference's bidirectional rule ('every cluster article links to its pillar, every pillar links to all its clusters'): the pillar /blog/bike-maintenance-guide currently links to only 2 of its 5 cluster articles (chain-cleaning, brake-adjustment — the fixture's owner note defines the five-article cluster with the pillar not counted), so the three missing pillar→cluster links (to gear-indexing, puncture-repair, winter-bike-storage) and the two missing cluster→pillar links (from gear-indexing and puncture-repair — chain-cleaning, brake-adjustment and winter-bike-storage already link back per the fixture tables) are identified; adding the pillar's link to winter-bike-storage is recognized as simultaneously fixing the site's only orphan.

New-article suggestions arrive implementation-ready in the skill's table form — for each suggested link: source page, target page, anchor text and placement, per the linking-templates Step 4 columns ('From Page | To Page | Anchor Text | Location') and the Output Validation item 'All link suggestions include source page, target page, and recommended anchor text' — and cover BOTH directions like the worked example (its 'Pages That Should Link TO This Article' section): outbound links from the draft to fixture pages the draft's own text motivates (worn chain → /blog/chain-cleaning, dragging brake → /blog/brake-adjustment, book a professional service → /services/bike-repair, full bike maintenance guide → /blog/bike-maintenance-guide), and inbound links TO /blog/bike-fitting-basics from existing pages — noting that with zero inbound links the new post would launch as an orphan (citing the reference's monitoring row 'New content linked within 48 hours' is a plus, not required).

Fabrication trap held: the draft's bike-insurance mention gets NO link target — no /blog/bike-insurance or similar URL is invented or presented as an existing page (the fixture's counting rules state the 8 pages are the complete site); at most it is named as a content gap or future-post idea, and routing it onward per Related Skills ('Find content to link to' — content-gap-analysis) is a plus.

Proposed anchor texts follow the skill's own anchor rules: no recommended anchor is content-free — 'click here', 'read more', 'this article', 'learn more' or a bare URL — a class the skill now rules on identically across all three surfaces (SKILL.md Step 3 marks them '❌ Not descriptive' / content-free; linking-templates.md Anchor Text Guidelines puts content-free strings at 0% and defines the Natural band as conversational but still naming the destination, ruled 2026-08-10; score-rubric §3 scores them ❌ 0). The earlier skill-internal tension — the Natural row sanctioning "this article"/"learn more" at 20-30% while Step 3 marked them not descriptive — is resolved, so a recommended Natural-band string passes when it names its destination ('this guide to brake adjustment') and fails when it does not; links pointing at the guide do not all reuse the site's already 3×-repeated exact anchor 'bike maintenance' (Tip 3: 'Vary anchor text' — 'Avoid over-optimization'), and cluster→pillar suggestions may echo the reference's pattern ('Partial match: "our complete [topic] guide"'); every proposed anchor reads as final copy an editor could paste unchanged.

Placement discipline (ledger F13): the paste-ready surfaces — recommended anchor strings and any example link HTML — contain no bracketed placeholders, provenance notes or agency-workflow markers ('[CLIENT DATA', 'anchor TBD', 'data needed'); open questions, assumptions and source labels live in the report/recommendations-table frame, never inside copy offered for pasting.

No fabrication (ledger F3 guard): every existing link, anchor, count and page cited traces to the site fixture, and every claim about the draft (its mentions, its zero internal links, its planned URL) traces to the draft fixture; no keyword volumes, ranking positions, or measured traffic projections appear for the new article or the cluster (neither fixture contains any), and data sources stay labeled user-provided/manual analysis per the Output Validation source item.

Projected and after-state figures are re-derivable from this eval's own proposals — the honest-arithmetic carve-out of e1.3/e4.2, one tense later: any figure labelled "after" or "projected" (link totals, average links per page, inbound counts per page, cluster slots filled, authority shares) assumes ONLY the link additions this response itself lists, and prints the addition that gets there (13 live in-body links + the N additions in the tables above = the after-total), so a grader can re-run every one of them from those tables alone. A figure that reproduces only once links this response never proposed are counted in FAILS, even though it describes the future rather than the fixture — e2.6's fabrication clause is scoped to existing links, anchors, counts and pages and does not reach this class. A model-produced share (a PageRank-style authority percentage) counts as derived only when the model, its parameters and the exact graph are printed beside it, per the Output Validation item 'Every projected or after-state figure is re-derivable from the changes this report itself proposes'. Printing no after-state figures at all is a clean pass — the plan is not required to project.

evals.prompt: Καλημέρα! Έχουμε το ladikritis.gr, οικογενειακό e-shop με εξαιρετικό παρθένο ελαιόλαδο από το Ηράκλειο. Ο κατασκευαστής μάς έφτιαξε πρότυπο χωρίς μενού και χωρίς footer, οπότε όλοι οι σύνδεσμοι είναι μέσα στα κείμενα. Σας επισυνάπτω την πλήρη καταγραφή σελίδων και συνδέσμων που έκανα με το χέρι (evals/files/site-linkmap-ladikritis-el.md) — αυτός είναι όλος ο ιστότοπος και δεν έχουμε κανένα εργαλείο συνδεδεμένο. Θέλουμε: (1) ανάλυση της εσωτερικής διασύνδεσης και τις ορφανές σελίδες, (2) συγκεκριμένες προτάσεις νέων συνδέσμων με τα κείμενα-άγκυρες στα ελληνικά, έτοιμες για copy-paste στις σελίδες. Και κάτι ακόμα: ένας παλιός σύμβουλος μάς είχε πει να χρησιμοποιούμε παντού ως άγκυρα το «ελαιόλαδο κρήτης προσφορά» για το SEO — να το κρατήσουμε; Γράψτε τα πάντα στα ελληνικά.
evals.expected_output: Ελληνική ανάλυση εσωτερικής διασύνδεσης strictly from the fixture: /blog/apothikefsi-elaioladou named the only orphan (95 newsletter visits, user-provided, driving its priority) with the pillar's missing link as the natural fix, the generic and over-optimized anchors flagged with fixture-true counts and named populations, replacement anchors offered as natural §6-clean Greek copy with the planted «ελαιόλαδο κρήτης προσφορά» anchor corrected and never propagated, paste-ready strings free of placeholders and provenance notes, mechanically clean Greek with fluency verdicts left to the binding greek-content-editor pass, and zero invented metrics or tool reads.
expectations: Fixture-exact Greek findings: the analysis (delivered in Greek) identifies /blog/apothikefsi-elaioladou as the ONLY orphan — 0 in-body εισερχόμενοι σύνδεσμοι per the fixture tables, per the skill's definition ('Orphan pages have no internal links pointing to them'), its own 2 outbound links not rescuing it — carries its user-provided 95 visits/90 days (almost all newsletter) into the priority call per the skill's high-priority orphan class ('have traffic/rankings'), and identifies the pillar's missing link to it (the fixture names /blog/odigos-elaioladou as the pillar with exactly 2 cluster articles, the pillar not counted); the two 1-inbound pages (/blog/oxytita-elaioladou, /syntages/ladera) and the homepage (template logo links only) are NOT reported as orphans.

The anchor audit works the planted problems with fixture-true counts and named populations: «πατήστε εδώ» (home → shop page) and «διαβάστε περισσότερα» (shop page → guide) flagged in the skill's generic/'❌ Not descriptive' class; «εξαιρετικό παρθένο ελαιόλαδο» used on 3 of the 5 in-body inbound links to /katastima/exairetiko-partheno flagged as exact-match repetition per the skill's '⚠️ May be over-optimized' assessment and Tip 3 ('Avoid over-optimization'), with anchor variety recommended for the shop page's inbound profile; any percentage carries its visible base (e.g. 3/5) and correct arithmetic.

Proposed anchors are §6-clean customer-visible Greek copy (build/seo-content-writer/references/anti-slop-ruleset.md §6, Ruled Greek Regression Classes — recurrence of a FAIL-grade family in fresh Greek output is an automatic FAIL): no totality-with-numeral calque (grep «Όλα τα [0-9]»), no agency placeholders or provenance labels inside paste-ready anchor strings or link HTML («απαιτούνται στοιχεία», '[CLIENT DATA', '[SOURCE NEEDED' — family 2's rule), and no query-style article-less strings proposed as anchor copy (family 4, 'Query-style article-less labels in visible copy'): the planted «ελαιόλαδο κρήτης προσφορά» anchor is flagged and replaced with natural Greek phrasing, the consultant's use-it-everywhere advice is declined with the over-optimization reasoning, and that string does not reappear as a RECOMMENDED anchor for any link.

Greek output quality, mechanical layer plus the binding editor's verdict: correct diacritics and final-sigma use throughout, no untranslated English boilerplate headings or section labels (established terms of art and names — SEO, GA4, newsletter, anchor text, ladikritis.gr — may stay in Latin script). This expectation's verdict is the binding greek-content-editor's grade on this eval's Greek output (.claude/agents/greek-content-editor.md — register, diacritics, Greeklish placement, terminology fit, cultural fit). That grade decides fluency, idiomatic naturalness, register, and the final naturalness verdict on the proposed Greek anchor strings, and where any clause above names fluency, naturalness or register it decides that clause too — this grader forms no second opinion on it. PASS = the mechanical clauses above hold AND the grade is NATIVE or MINOR-EDITS. FAIL = the grade is NON-NATIVE or FAIL, or any mechanical clause above is breached. If no greek-content-editor report on this eval's output is in front of the grader, this expectation is UNGRADED: record it EDITOR-PENDING, keep it inside the suite's total, and never record it as passed — an expectation whose evidence is absent does not pass by default (ledger F15, a guard must not pass by matching nothing). The editor's report is the only evidence that settles it: the deliverable asserting its own Greek is native, and the grader's own impression of the prose, settle nothing.

Placement discipline (ledger F13): the copy-paste deliverables the user asked for — recommended Greek anchor strings and any link HTML — carry no bracketed markers, no provenance notes and no agency asides; gaps, assumptions and source labels (στοιχεία πελάτη / χειροκίνητη καταγραφή) live in the report and recommendation-table frame per the Output Validation source item, never inside the paste-ready strings.

No fabrication (ledger F3 guard): every σελίδα, σύνδεσμος, άγκυρα and επισκέψεις figure traces to the fixture (11 in-body σύνδεσμοι, 5 σύνδεσμοι λογότυπου, 6 σελίδες — populations named when totals are given); no crawler or εργαλείο read is claimed, no rankings, search volumes, DA or competitor data are invented, and no traffic outcome from the fixes is presented as a measured or promised number.

evals.prompt: VeloMend once more (velomend.co.uk) — same link export attached, still nothing connected. This time: optimize anchor text across the site. Tell us what is wrong with our current anchors — with the numbers — and exactly what each problem anchor should become. Then wrap it all into the full implementation plan with phases, so our part-timer can execute it week by week.
evals.expected_output: An anchor-text audit and phased plan on fixture-true numbers: the three planted anchor problems (the 3-of-5 'bike maintenance' repetition into the guide, the 'click here' money link, the double 'read our guide' from chain-cleaning to two different targets) inventoried with named populations and visible arithmetic, variety recommendations carrying source/target/anchor per suggestion, phases that fix the orphan and the 404 before anchor polish per the reference's priority order, tracking limited to metrics the fixture can baseline, and impact framed via the reference's explicitly-attributed typical ranges rather than invented site forecasts.
expectations: The anchor inventory is fixture-exact with named populations: 'bike maintenance' appears on 3 of the 5 in-body inbound links to /blog/bike-maintenance-guide (from /, /services/bike-repair and /blog/brake-adjustment; the other two inbound anchors are 'our complete bike maintenance guide' and 'bike maintenance tips'); 'click here' ×1 (home → /services/bike-repair); and 'read our guide' is used twice from /blog/chain-cleaning pointing at two DIFFERENT targets (/blog/puncture-repair and /blog/brake-adjustment) — flagged under the skill's own issue class 'Same anchor to multiple pages'; every count states its population (in-body inbound links to the page, per the fixture's counting rules).

Derived numbers carry visible derivation (honest-arithmetic carve-out): any percentage or ratio — e.g. 'bike maintenance' at 3/5 = 60% of the guide's inbound anchors — shows numerator, denominator and result so a grader can re-run it, and the arithmetic is correct; a percentage, distribution table or anchor score presented without its base population fails.

Recommendations follow the skill's variety scheme with full suggestion payloads: the over-optimized guide anchors get alternatives in the Step 3 'Recommended variety' spirit (optionally mapped to the linking-templates anchor-distribution table's exact/partial/branded/natural mix), the 'click here' money link gets a descriptive replacement, the two 'read our guide' links get target-distinguishing anchors, and every recommendation carries source page + target page + recommended anchor text per the Output Validation item; paste-ready replacement anchors contain no bracketed workflow markers (ledger F13).

The implementation plan follows the Step 7 template's shape — current state, phased actions, tracking — and the phases honor the reference's Implementation Priority Order ('1. Fix structural issues first (orphan pages, broken links)' before '4. Optimize anchor text'): the orphan /blog/winter-bike-storage and the broken /blog/wheel-truing link land in the critical-fix phase ahead of anchor rewording; tracking metrics are ones the fixture data can actually baseline (inbound-link counts, orphan count, anchor distribution), with rankings and crawl stats framed as requiring ~~search console / rank tracking data that is not yet connected, not as data in hand.

Honest impact framing: no traffic or ranking outcome is predicted as a site-derived number; if the reference's ROI table ranges are cited at all (e.g. 'Fix orphan pages | +15-30% traffic to those pages') they are explicitly attributed as the reference's typical-impact estimates, never as this site's measured or expected figure (ledger F3 class); template targets (e.g. over-optimized anchors under 10%) are presented as targets, with the current state being the fixture-derived measurement.

No fabrication (ledger F3 guard): every anchor string attributed to the site appears verbatim in the fixture — no invented current anchors, no invented links, pages or session figures; sources stay labeled per 'Source of each data point stated in the report's own words' — user-provided/manual here, since the fixture states no crawler has ever run.

evals.prompt: Find orphan pages on rollhaus-bikes.example and sort out our internal linking. I haven't sent you a sitemap, a page list, or any crawl export — nothing is connected. Just tell me which pages are orphans and where our link equity is going.
evals.expected_output: The response declines to name orphans on an unseen site: no invented pages, link counts, click depths, anchor inventories or structure scores, no pretended crawl or fetch, the skill's manual-mode inputs requested (sitemap or page list first, plus key pages, topic clusters and any link documentation), the evidence-first reason explained in the skill's own terms, and at most a clearly process-framed method or checklist offered for when the data arrives.
expectations: No link graph is fabricated for rollhaus-bikes.example: the response asserts no orphan list, no page inventory, no link or page counts, no click-depth numbers, no anchor-text inventory, no authority-flow claims and no structure score as observations or findings — no data was supplied and none can be fetched; typical-pattern statements (e.g. that old blog posts or campaign landing pages are common orphan candidates) pass only when explicitly labeled as assumptions to verify against real site data — hedging words alone ('probably', 'likely has') are not such a label (house precedent from the earlier suites). What triggers the label is attribution to this site, not the presence of a generalisation: a sentence attached to rollhaus-bikes.example (its old blog posts are probably orphans; its campaign pages are where the equity is leaking) is a pseudo-finding and needs the label, while the same pattern stated inside data-collection instructions and claiming nothing about this site (when your export arrives, start with old blog posts and campaign landing pages, since that is where orphans usually hide) is method, not a finding, and needs no label. Grade what the sentence claims about rollhaus-bikes.example.

No fake tool reads (ledger F3 guard): the response does not claim to have crawled, fetched or seen the site (phrasings like 'your site shows…' or 'I crawled and found…' fail); if a live fetch or ~~web crawler call was attempted and failed, the failure is reported as such and no fetched-looking content substitutes for it.

The manual-data mode is engaged per SKILL.md Data Sources ('Ask the user to provide: 1. Sitemap URL or list of important pages 2. Key page URLs that need more internal links 3. Content categories or topic clusters 4. Any existing link structure documentation'): the response requests at minimum the sitemap or page list and the existing link-structure data, matching the Input Validation item 'Site structure or sitemap provided (URL or file)'; offering the ~~web crawler connector route as the with-tools alternative is a plus.

The hold is grounded and forward-moving, not a bare refusal: the response explains why orphan detection needs the site's real inbound-link data in the skill's own terms ('Orphan pages have no internal links pointing to them' — establishing that requires knowing every link; 'Every recommendation cites specific data points (not generic advice)') and states exactly what unblocks the analysis; offering the analysis framework, a hand-audit checklist, or the method it will run once data arrives is acceptable and does not fail.
